name: Spiral
description: Phi-ratio growth curve representing natural proportionality and temporal unfolding.

core_attributes.pattern: logarithmic expansion, fractal proportionality, growth path

scope.definition: Proportion of naturally-occurring logarithmic spirals in biological specimens (shells, phyllotaxis patterns, horns, plant meristems) whose growth ratio matches φ (≈1.618) within a 5% tolerance, as determined by curve-fitting to morphological measurement data.

evidence.source: Livio (2002) 'The Golden Ratio', Broadway Books — survey of 200+ biological and physical cases; Mitchison (1977) 'Phyllotaxis and the Fibonacci Series', Science 196:270-275; D'Arcy Thompson (1917) 'On Growth and Form', Cambridge.
cross_domain_examples: sunflower seed head Fibonacci packing (55/89 or 89/144 spiral arms)
galaxy spiral arm curvature (approximate; varies by galaxy type)
DNA double helix major groove: 34Å pitch / 21Å width ≈ φ
ram horn and bovid horn growth curve

scope.falsifiability: If a class of biological spiral structures is found where growth ratios cluster reproducibly around a different constant (e.g., √2 or e), the φ-spiral as primary biological growth attractor requires revision.
scope.measurement_limits: φ is an attractor, not a constraint — real spirals show ±5-10% deviation. The ratio emerges from iterative proportional growth, not a hardcoded geometric blueprint. Galaxy arms are approximate and vary by type.
